quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them. These are smaller and harder to spot than cars. They may move faster and have dim lights. Always watch for motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians to prevent crashes.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded roads. Areas under trees or buildings freeze faster than other roads. They also dry last.

questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show you are turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals don't work, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk your horn so others know to get out of your way.
Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. It is unlawful not to stop.

questions.question: Taking drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases the risk of a crash.
Is not more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces the effects of alcohol on driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can harm how your brain works and affect your driving. Mixing alcohol with drugs increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for things in your car, reading, looking around, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and looking at gauges regularly. These safe habits keep you focused.

questions.question: How alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment depends on:

options.text: Whether you drink beer instead of wine.
Whether you drink wine instead of beer.
Whether you drink hard ciders or mixed drinks.
How much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can harm your reflexes and judgment. The type of drink does not matter. Only the amount of alcohol in your blood matters.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Turn your wheel toward oncoming traffic.
Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the direction of the skid.

questions.question: You cannot safely pass on a two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You cannot safely pass on a two-lane street unless you can clearly see ahead, you can get back to your lane before meeting oncoming cars, and your car can go fast enough to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: It does not matter which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: A person who drives much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let following cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic can be dangerous. On a two-lane road with traffic backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other vehicles pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when road conditions require it.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe driving. You should:

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you can afford it.
Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that may affect safe driving should be fixed as soon as possible. Fix defects before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce
questions.explanation: When turning, reduce your speed so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the maximum speed limit in a business or residential district is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: In business and residential districts, the maximum speed limit is 25 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted. Always follow the posted speed limit.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving in both directions ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely to be:

options.text: A person involved with a traffic study.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind person.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog. These are signs of a blind person.

questions.question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. From 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people or vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Orange diamond-shaped signs with black letters warn of work zones on the road. They tell drivers that workers are on or near the highway.

questions.question: When approaching a flashing yellow light, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light is a warning of a hazard. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Driving while distracted by any activity:

options.text: Usually slows down the driver's reaction time to hazards.
Usually causes the driver to drive faster.
Is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually slows down the driver's reaction time to hazards.
questions.explanation: Distractions make drivers react more slowly to traffic and hazards. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: You may turn right on a solid red traffic light:

options.text: When there is a sign prohibiting turning right on red.
Before pedestrians have crossed the crosswalk.
Before coming to a complete stop.
After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you stop completely and yield to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.
questions.explanation: You may turn right on a red light after making a complete stop. Only turn if it is safe and if there is no sign blocking the turn. Give the right-of-way to other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian has the legal right.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always yield the right-of-way, even if the pedestrian is wrong.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter the situation. It is your job as a driver to watch for pedestrians and give them the right-of-way at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: When you are being tailgated:

options.text: Move to the right lane if one is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until the road ahead is clear and slowly reduce your speed to let the tailgater pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you and a right lane is open, move over to it. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and then slowly reduce your speed. This lets the tailgater pass you. Never brake suddenly because this increases the risk of being hit from behind.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right.
